Test uses typical values (n = 105 and edge 0->1) and does not validate boundary conditions such as 0, n-1, negative indices, or out-of-range indices. No explicit boundary tests are present.

The test class does not define helper methods or constants for repeated setup. There is hardcoded data (n = 105, magic value 1333) inside the test and no extracted helper to improve reuse or readability.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method contains multiple comment lines, a try-catch, an instanceof branch, and multiple assertions, making it longer and more complex than recommended. It exhibits control flow (try/catch and if) raising cyclomatic complexity above 1-2.

The test contains multiple substantive assertions verifying non-null result, vertex count for transpose (when applicable), existence of reversed edge, and that the original graph's vertex count is unchanged — checking multiple properties of behavior.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out @Test methods in the provided class; all tests appear active and runnable.
The method includes a comment 'Req: GRAPH-09' documenting the requirement linked to this test, providing traceability between test and requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout attribute (@Test(timeout = 4000)) which is an explicit timing constraint; therefore an explicit performance-related annotation is present and counted as compliant per the decision rules.

The test method is named 'test8', which is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions such as methodName_scenario_expectedResult. The name does not communicate purpose or expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: No explicit auto-generated comments ('Auto-generated by...') or repetitive generated names are present. Although EvoSuite imports appear, there are no clear signs of heavy code generation in this single test method, so this practice is not applicable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given-When-Then style comments and demonstrates considered scenario coverage for the transpose operation, indicating thoughtful test design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API methods (Grafo constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices, existeAresta) and does not access private fields or use reflection, so it verifies behavior via public interfaces.
Assertions use specific methods (assertNotNull, assertEquals, assertTrue) and include descriptive failure messages for many assertions, improving diagnostic clarity.
The test uses concise Given-When-Then comments and class-level Javadoc explaining intent; comments explain rationale rather than restate obvious code, so they add value without clutter.
The test uses no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no System.currentTimeMillis(), no Thread.sleep()) and relies on local state, so results should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test modifies only local in-memory graph state and does not persist data to external resources or modify static/global state; no cleanup is required.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing classification for selective execution and indicating appropriate labeling.
